text:
harper: follow-up on rollout metadata hints. small but important ops/security wrinkle: we need to decide a salt policy for compat fingerprints so hashes cane used safely across tenants and for public model catalog. sketching options and tradeoffs.

harper: quick sketch of fields we discussed earlier (for context):
```
anchor: translate-lite@2026-11-02
compat_hint: minor
compat_fingerprint: blake2b:abcd1234...
```

harper: option A = global salt (fast, searchable across tenants). option B = per-tenant salt (privacy-preserving, avoids cross-tenant correlation). option C = ephemeral salt per-ingest (max privacy, no cross-indexing).

sam: my gut: per-tenant salt seems best for enterprise customers (can't correlate their private models with public catalog). but ops cost: you can't easily route by fingerprint across tenants if salted differently.

lucy: +1 for per-tenant. also: need a documented salt-rotation policy. if salt rotates, old fingerprints must be revokable/backfilled. we should give a TTL window where both old and new fingerprints accepted for handshake-fallback.

noah: ops: if we go per-tenant, backfill and cross-tenant telemetry become harder. search for identical tokenizer-shape across tenants becomes impossible without re-hashing all with a global salt. Is that required?
harper: we only use fingerprint locally in resolvers as tie-breaks. cross-tenant dedupe isn't a must. but for public model catalog (open models) we might want global salt to help dedupe and metrics. maybe hybrid: per-tenant for private uploads, global for public models.

sam: hybrid complicates client resolver logic: resolver must know whether fingerprint is tenant-salted or global. we can expose a small `fingerprint_scope` field: `global|tenant|ephemeral`. examples below.

harper: example schema snippet: 
```
{
  "anchor": "summarize@2026-11-02",
  "compat_hint": "compatible_minor",
  "compat_fingerprint": "b2:5e4a9c...",
  "fingerprint_scope": "tenant",  // global | tenant | ephemeral
  "fingerprint_alg": "blake2b128",
  "note": "salted per-tenant; resolver uses only for tie-breaks"
}
```

lucy: good. also require a `fingerprint_salt_id` on writes so we can rotate salts and keep audits. salt id is internal only and not exposed to customers. when rotating, onboarding writes the new salt_id and compute and we accept both salt versions for N days.

noah: security nuance: we must avoid leaking salt values in logs or telemetry. telemetry can emit `fingerprint_scope` and `hint_used` but never the raw fingerprint. also redact any debug dumps.

sam: perf: per-tenant compute is trivial at ingest time, but backfill across thousands of tenant models can be heavy. plan: rate-limited backfill with priority: public models first, then customers who opted-in to fast backfill. provide a customer CLI to request recompute.

harper: pinning interaction: pinned pools must ignore fingerprint scope for eviction decisions. we agreed hints only affect intra-pool selection; pinned eviction remains lease/anchor-driven. add a test to ensure no eviction path uses fingerprint as input.

lucy: telemetry items: `rollout.hint_considered`, `rollout.hint_applied`, `rollout.fingerprint_scope` tag, `rollout.fingerprint_mismatch` counter. no raw fingerprint in metrics.

noah: policy for public catalog: public models default to `fingerprint_scope=global` and use documented, versioned salt (rotate infrequently with deprecation window). private uploads default to `tenant`. ephemeral used only for one-off ingest where customer asks to disable future correlation.

sam: migration notes: 1) add `fingerprint_scope`, `fingerprint_alg`, and `fingerprint_salt_id` nullable fields to registry API. 2) default existing models to `fingerprint_scope=global` for public and `tenant` for private (we'll detect by visibility flag), with an initial backfill dry-run to estimate costs. 3) resolver change behind feature flag; backfill and salt-rotation behind ops schedule.

harper: testing: unit tests for resolver that handle mixed-scope catalogs, sim tests with intentionally wrong salt mapping, and e2e canary that routes small percentage to signal-aware resolver. add regression test ensuring no pinned-eviction triggered by hint.

lucy: legal/compliance: get privacy sign-off for per-tenant salt in writing. especially for regulated customers, document that fingerprinting uses only tokenizer/config shapes and is not reversible. add a KB entry for customers explaining salt choices and opt-out steps.

noah: actionables: harper -> draft registry schema patch text including `fingerprint_scope` + `fingerprint_salt_id`; sam -> backfill cost spike and plan; lucy -> privacy/legal note + telemetry spec; harper -> resolver FF + unit tests. ETA next Wed.

rollout-bot: ACTIONS: 1) harper: post PR linking schema diff. 2) sam: perf spike report. 3) lucy: privacy note. 4) all: verification tests.

harper: thanks all. i'll post the PR and link the spike results here. :thumbsup:
